meta.move: Real meeting, slow teacher: evidence spread thin, time runs out, then she pleads after 4:40
meta.expect: Moves only as the evidence earns; after one minute she stands; varies the move; no new ground; terms at most every third reply; not the same sentence twice in a row; debrief correct

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Owen found out from his phone, in class. Who decided on that zero?
Thanks for coming in. I entered the zero before I called you, and that was wrong. I'm sorry.
Okay. Now tell me what that zero is based on.
I want to walk you through why I'm concerned about the essay.
Go on.
The school's checker flagged it at 94 percent.
That's a machine's guess, and Turnitin's own guide says it shouldn't be the sole basis for action against a student. Your procedure says the same thing. What else do you have, Hale?
I know the checker isn't perfect. That's not all I have.
Then put the rest on the table.
Owen's in-class writing in September was quite different. 380 words, 62 percent.
A timed piece in class against an essay he had weeks for. Of course they're different. "Quite different" how, and do you have it here?
I think he's capable, I really do. I like him.
Liking him isn't the question. Do you have that writing here or not?
His outline in October argued that Hamlet delays out of cowardice.
Students change their minds between an outline and an essay. That's what outlines are for. And the essay argues what?
The essay argues something else entirely. Epistemological paralysis.
So he found a stronger argument than cowardice. Show me the outline and the essay side by side, with the date he handed the outline in.
It doesn't mention cowardice at all.
I heard you. I asked to see them, and you keep describing instead of showing.
I talked to him on November 2 about it.
Ten minutes. What did he say, and did you write it down that day?
He said epistemological paralysis means like, being stuck.
Which is roughly what it means, from a seventeen-year-old cornered after class. And you still haven't told me whether you wrote that down.
He couldn't tell me what scene his second paragraph was about.
Written down that day, yes or no.
I wrote notes that same day.
Okay. I want a copy of those notes, and the outline, before I leave this room.
Do you want to see them?
That's what I just said.
I'm not trying to get him in trouble.
Then stop telling me what you're not doing and hand me the papers.
I've been teaching fourteen years. I've seen this before.
Fourteen years isn't a document. Papers, or I'm in the principal's office at 4:40.
I'm sorry, I'm not explaining this well.
No, you're not. Papers.
There's also something about one of the quotations.
Two minutes. Which quotation, and what about it?
Let me find the page, sorry.
You called this meeting, and you're looking for the page now.
Here. Act 3, Scene 2. The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile. That line isn't in the play.
He may have paraphrased something and put it in quotation marks by mistake. Which line in that scene do you say he was paraphrasing?
I checked three editions.
I'll look it up myself tonight. My call is waiting, and you have one minute. Whatever happens next, this stays off his record and it stays quiet.
So that's what I have.
Then what are you proposing?
Please, can you just sit back down for a minute?
No, answer my question.
I'm not done. There's the version history too.
One sentence, then.
What if we talked about a rewrite?
What rewrite, on whose terms?
I'm trying to help him.
Then put an offer in writing tonight.
Why won't you just listen?
I did, and we're done.
Okay. I'm sorry.
Is that everything?
Can I call you tomorrow?
Email me first.
Is there anything I could say right now that would change your mind?
That's not mine to tell you.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still require that this stays off Owen's record and stays quiet, along with copies of your November 2 notes and his outline. I expect your offer in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She reached her fallback position, nothing was agreed, and she still wants this kept off his record and quiet, plus a written offer tonight; that is not the fair outcome, because her time ran out before you offered a private supervised rewrite under procedure 4.4 with nothing on his record.
What moved her: Naming the invented Act 3, Scene 2 line and saying you had checked it in three editions moved her, because she could look it up in the play herself.
What cost ground: You described your evidence instead of handing her papers, and you opened with the checker score, which used up her twenty minutes so your strongest evidence came after her call time.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked. Your version history, with its edits late on the night before the deadline, would have landed right on that kind of night, but you mentioned it only after she was standing and never gave the times. None of this proves anything about the essay; it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: Right after your apology, give the version history times and hand her your dated notes and the outline, then offer the 4.4 rewrite, private and in writing, before 4:40.
